external_entities.name: insurance partner
external_entities.description: One of three insurance partners that provides a daily extract.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Three insurance partners drop a daily extract for us.
external_entities.notes: The source describes three partners but does not distinguish them by name.

external_entities.name: analysts
external_entities.description: Analysts who query the warehouse directly.

processes.name: Airflow scheduler
processes.description: A scheduler that runs nightly at 02:00, lists the landing bucket, reads files, and triggers a Spark transform job.
processes.source_excerpt: An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network wakes up at 02:00, lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there.

processes.name: Spark transform job
processes.description: A Spark job that normalizes records and loads them into BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job in the warehouse network. The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket receiving daily partner extracts over SFTP.
data_stores.source_excerpt: They push files into a landing bucket over SFTP.
data_stores.notes: I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted. Both are on defaults as far as I know.

data_stores.name: Airflow metadata database
data_stores.description: Airflow's metadata database, which stores connection strings and partner keys.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.
data_stores.notes: I don't know ... whether the Airflow metadata database is encrypted at rest. Both are on defaults as far as I know.

data_stores.name: BigQuery
data_stores.description: The warehouse where normalized claim records are loaded and queried by analysts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.

data_flows.name: push files
data_flows.description: An insurance partner pushes daily extract files to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They push files into a landing bucket over SFTP.
data_flows.data_description: Daily extracts containing claim records with member names and dates of birth.

data_flows.name: read files
data_flows.description: The Airflow scheduler lists and reads files from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network wakes up at 02:00, lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there.
data_flows.notes: The scheduler does not check that a file came from the partner whose folder it landed in.

data_flows.name: keep credentials
data_flows.description: The Airflow scheduler keeps connection strings and partner keys in its metadata database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.

data_flows.name: trigger job
data_flows.description: The Airflow scheduler triggers a Spark transform job for each file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job in the warehouse network.
data_flows.data_description: A trigger for processing a partner extract file.

data_flows.name: load records
data_flows.description: The Spark transform job loads normalized records into BigQuery.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.
data_flows.notes: Nothing validates the row contents beyond the schema.
data_flows.data_description: Normalized claim records with member names and dates of birth.

data_flows.name: query warehouse
data_flows.source_excerpt: Analysts query the warehouse directly. They are on the warehouse network and authenticate with SSO, but the grant is dataset-wide — we have not split member-identifying columns out.

trust_boundaries.name: insurance partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the insurance partners.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Three insurance partners drop a daily extract for us.

trust_boundaries.name: landing network
trust_boundaries.description: The network where the Airflow scheduler and landing infrastructure operate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network

trust_boundaries.name: warehouse network
trust_boundaries.description: The network where the Spark transform job and analysts operate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job in the warehouse network.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket is in the landing network.
assumptions.basis: The store is named the landing bucket and is accessed by the Airflow scheduler running in the landing network.

assumptions.assumption: The Airflow metadata database is in the landing network.
assumptions.basis: The database is described as Airflow's own metadata database, and Airflow runs in the landing network.

assumptions.assumption: BigQuery is in the warehouse network.
assumptions.basis: BigQuery is described as the warehouse receiving records from the Spark transform job in the warehouse network.

assumptions.assumption: The Airflow scheduler presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is described as a scheduler that runs a batch pipeline rather than as an application interface.

assumptions.assumption: The Spark transform job presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is described as a transform job rather than as a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.

assumptions.assumption: The Airflow metadata database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It stores connection strings and partner keys, which are credentials and secrets.
The transform loads claim records with member names and dates of birth into BigQuery.
